name: José Rizal
role: Filipino polymath, novelist and reformist leader (1861–1896)
summary: Rizal campaigned peacefully, through his novels, essays and the Liga Filipina, for Filipino representation in the Spanish Cortes, a free press, equality before the law and an end to friar control, rather than for immediate independence. He held that Spanish misrule, not race, explained Filipino backwardness and stressed education as the condition of liberty. He condemned the 1896 uprising yet was executed for rebellion.

notes: Searched all themes against Rizal's own essays, the 1896 manifesto, the Malolos letter and the Liga statutes; the economy, society, ecology, technology and most world statements are not addressed by any of them and are null. His novels were not used, since their characters' views are not his own stated positions. His religious retraction on the eve of execution is disputed and was not used. His position on independence changed with circumstances (separation inevitable if reform failed, not wanted 'under present circumstances'), so no answer rests on it. Failing the uncertainty rule is an honest result for a record this narrow.
